summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that sets up a LimeSurvey application with a MySQL database backend. It defines two services that work together: a web application container and a database container, with the app configured to wait for the database to be healthy before starting.

explanations.5: This specifies which pre-built Docker image to use for the LimeSurvey service — think of it like selecting a specific version of software from a repository.
explanations.6: The double-percent notation (%%app_name=limesurvey-app%%) is a template variable that gets replaced with an actual value when this file is processed, allowing the same config to be reused with different names.
explanations.7: This tells Docker to automatically restart this container if it crashes or stops, keeping the service running continuously.
explanations.10: This environment variable tells the LimeSurvey app how to find its database — it uses another template variable that will be substituted with the actual database service name.
explanations.19: This maps port 8080 on your host machine to port 80 inside the container, so you can access the web app by visiting localhost:8080 in your browser.
explanations.21: The app won't start until the database service is not only running but has passed its health check, ensuring the database is actually ready to accept connections.
explanations.33: This health check command periodically runs 'mysqladmin ping' to verify the database is responsive; if it fails too many times, Docker marks the container as unhealthy.
